raw_case_text:
A 37-year-old gentleman with underlying human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) diagnosed in June 2015 was under infectious disease clinic follow-up from another center. He was started on combined antiretroviral therapy (tenofovir-emtricitabine and efavirenz) since diagnosis but defaulted treatment a month prior to his admission to our center. His CD4 count upon diagnosis was 20 cells/microliter and serum creatinine of 108 micromol/L. After 12 months of treatment, his HIV viral load was less than 20 cells/L, and CD4 increased to 178 cells/microliter and serum creatinine of 193 micromol/L. During his follow-up in February 2017, serum creatinine rose markedly to 1051 micromol/L but remained asymptomatic; he was advised for admission and further investigation, but the patient refused due to some family issues.
He presented to our center in April 2017 with vomiting and gross hematuria for one week associated with abdominal pain and distention. He was also symptomatic of anemia. He had loss of weight and loss of appetite. He had good urine output (more than one liter in a day) and no frothy urine. He did not take any nephrotoxic drugs, that is, herbal supplementation or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. Clinically, he was pale, and bilateral kidneys were ballotable and massively enlarged with an irregular surface and hard in consistency. There were no hepatomegaly and splenomegaly. Peripheral lymph nodes were not palpable as well.
Blood investigations showed hemoglobin of 3.7 g/L (normochromic and normocytic), total white count of 7.6 x 109/L, lymphocyte count of 1.7 x 109/L, and neutrophil count of 5.4 x 109/L and urea of 65.6 mmol/L, serum creatinine of 1630 micromol/L, potassium of 5.4 mmol/L, sodium of 132 mmol/L, hyperphosphatemia of 3.70 mmol/L, and corrected serum calcium of 2.48 mmol/L. Venous blood gas showed metabolic acidosis with pH of 7.18 and bicarbonate of 11 mmol/L. Urinalysis showed urine protein 2 + (0.75 g/L) and blood 3 + (250 mu/L). An internal jugular double-lumen catheter was inserted, and hemodialysis was initiated. Ultrasound abdomen (Figure 1) and 4-phase renal computed tomography (CT) (Figure 2) were done.
The ultrasound showed enlarged bilateral kidneys with calculus, and his 4-phase renal CT showed diffuse nonenhancing hypodense lesion in both renal parenchyma. The lesion at the right kidney extends medially to the paraaortic region, forming another hypodense mass component, measuring 6.4 cm x 8.1 cm x 11 cm. The mass is displacing the branches of the aorta, duodenum, and pancreas anteriorly. Subcentimetre nodes were seen in the mesenteric and inguinal region. In view of definite diagnosis cannot be made via imaging, a renal biopsy was arranged. Histopathology and immunochemistry result of left renal tissue showed diffuse large B cell lymphoma with the germinal center type (Figures 3-5).
A bone marrow aspirate and trephine (BMAT) was done and showed no bone marrow infiltration. Positron emission tomography CT scan (PET-CT) concluded extensive malignant lesion in the upper abdomen involving the kidneys, stomach, and pancreas. The liver, spleen, lungs, and brain have normal uptake. There were malignant lesions also found in the right cervical node, left tonsils, and posterior chest wall. Some small bone metastasis was also detected.
His repeat CD4 count was 84 cells/microliter, and the viral load was 6974 copies per ml. He was restarted on antiretroviral treatment: oral Kivexa (abacavir/lamivudine) 1 tab daily and oral efavirenz 600 mg daily, added oral trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole (Bactrim) 2 tablets daily as prophylaxis prior to starting chemotherapy. He underwent regular hemodialysis and was transfused with packed red blood cell. He was planned for standard treatment of rituximab-cyclophosphamide, hydroxydaunorubicin, Oncovin, and prednisone (R-CHOP), but the patient developed upper gastrointestinal bleed and succumbed to death before starting the chemotherapy.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 37-year-old male presenting with vomiting, gross hematuria, abdominal pain, and abdominal distension for one week.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a 1-week history of persistent vomiting, gross total hematuria, worsening abdominal pain, and abdominal distension, accompanied by fatigue, anorexia, and progressive weight loss. Two months prior, routine follow-up had shown asymptomatic severe azotemia for which he declined admission. Following arrival at the emergency department, he was found to have critical uremia and severe symptomatic anemia necessitating emergent vascular catheter placement and hemodialysis.
subjective.past_medical_history: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection diagnosed in June 2015 (baseline CD4 count 20 cells/microL, serum creatinine 108 micromol/L), treated with tenofovir, emtricitabine, and efavirenz until defaulting therapy one month prior to presentation; history of progressive non-oliguric renal impairment (serum creatinine rising from 193 micromol/L to 1,051 micromol/L in February 2017); denies ingestion of herbal or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agents.
subjective.review_of_systems: Vomiting, gross hematuria, abdominal fullness, profound weakness, anorexia, and weight loss; denies frothy urine, oliguria, fever, night sweats, or hemoptysis.

objective.physical_examination: General: Marked conjunctival and cutaneous pallor. Abdomen: Bilateral massive, hard, irregular, ballotable renal masses palpable in both flanks; absence of hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, or ascites. Lymph nodes: Peripheral cervical, axillary, and inguinal lymph nodes non-palpable.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count: Hemoglobin 3.7 g/dL (severe normocytic, normochromic anemia), total white cell count 7.6 x 10^9/L (neutrophils 5.4 x 10^9/L, lymphocytes 1.7 x 10^9/L). Renal & Electrolytes: Serum urea 65.6 mmol/L, serum creatinine 1,630 micromol/L, potassium 5.4 mmol/L, sodium 132 mmol/L, serum phosphate 3.70 mmol/L, corrected calcium 2.48 mmol/L. Venous blood gas: Metabolic acidosis with pH 7.18 and bicarbonate 11 mmol/L. Urinalysis: Protein 2+ (0.75 g/L), blood 3+ (250 erythrocytes/microL). Renal ultrasonography: Bilaterally enlarged kidneys with nephrolithiasis.
objective.advanced_workup: Four-phase contrast-enhanced abdominal CT: Diffuse, bilateral non-enhancing hypodense infiltrative lesions expanding the renal parenchyma bilaterally, with a medial retroperitoneal/paraaortic mass arising from the right kidney measuring 6.4 cm x 8.1 cm x 11.0 cm that displaced the aorta, duodenum, and pancreas anteriorly, along with subcentimeter mesenteric and inguinal lymphadenopathy. Left renal biopsy: Histopathology and immunohistochemistry demonstrated diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), germinal center B-cell subtype. Bone marrow aspirate and trephine biopsy: Uninvolved (no lymphomatous infiltration). Whole-body PET-CT: Widespread hypermetabolic malignancy involving bilateral kidneys, stomach, pancreas, right cervical lymph node, left tonsil, posterior chest wall, and osseous metastases, with sparing of liver, spleen, and brain.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Advanced human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection with virologic rebound (CD4 count 84 cells/microL, HIV RNA 6,974 copies/mL) presenting with Stage IV Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL, germinal center phenotype) causing bilateral renal lymphomatous infiltration, severe acute-on-chronic uremic renal failure, and profound anemia.
Plan & Outcome: Emergent internal jugular hemodialysis catheter inserted and intermittent hemodialysis initiated; supported with packed red blood cell transfusions. Antiretroviral therapy was re-initiated using a renally adjusted regimen of abacavir/lamivudine (Kivexa) and efavirenz, along with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (Bactrim) for Pneumocystis prophylaxis. Pre-chemotherapy workup for R-CHOP was arranged; however, the patient developed a catastrophic upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage and passed away prior to initiating antineoplastic therapy.
